title: CS-MT024-ClaudeInterrupt

scope.summary:
GOAL: Mid-turn interrupt of a RUNNING Claude Code session without killing it: emit a control_request interrupt line on the session's stdin, gated on the interrupt_receipt_v1 capability when the system/init capabilities array advertises it, behind an explicit feature flag, with a typed CapabilityMissing degradation and a guaranteed fallback path = MT-005 supervisor graceful stop (SIGTERM: aborts turn, kills bash tree, runs SessionEnd hooks, exit 143). The undocumented-protocol surface is kept to the ONE interrupt subtype — no other control subtypes may be emitted, referenced, or scaffolded.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: new file src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/claude_interrupt.rs (request constructor + gate + outcome types) + wiring into the session command surface next to the MT-023 injector; tests with scripted child; live proof.

SPEC:
1. Wire shape behind ONE constructor: `claude_interrupt_request_line(request_id: &str) -> String` producing a single serde-serialized JSON line + newline for the control_request interrupt (shape per the reverse-engineered protocol: a top-level control_request envelope whose request payload has subtype "interrupt"; Roasbeef claude-agent-sdk-go docs/cli-protocol.md, anthropics/claude-code#41665). The exact field spelling is pinned in this ONE function + its snapshot test, so a protocol drift is a one-line fix and MT-028 catches it. request_id is minted as Uuid::now_v7().to_string() (HBR-INT-008).
2. Feature flag: `claude_interrupt_enabled: bool` in the Claude adapter config (default OFF until MT-028 contract evidence exists). Flag OFF -> `InterruptOutcome::FeatureDisabled` and the caller is directed to the supervisor stop; the flag state is recorded on the outcome so ledger rows show WHY the soft path was skipped.
3. Capability gate: interrupt emission requires the session's MT-003 capability set to contain "interrupt_receipt_v1" (captured from system/init by MT-022). Capability absent -> typed `InterruptOutcome::CapabilityMissing` WITHOUT writing anything to stdin (never fire undocumented bytes at an unknown CLI). Capability present + flag on -> write the line via the MT-004 stdin writer, then await the interrupt receipt/turn-abort evidence in the stream (turn ends without a normal result completion for the aborted turn) within a bounded `interrupt_ack_timeout` (default 10s).
4. Outcomes are a closed set: `Interrupted { request_id, acked: bool }` (acked=true when receipt evidence observed; acked=false = timeout -> caller MUST escalate), `CapabilityMissing`, `FeatureDisabled`, `ChildGone`, `EscalatedToSupervisorStop { reason }`. There is NO silent path: every outcome is returned AND emitted to the MT-029 recording seam (no-op sink allowed until MT-029 lands, flagged in implementation result).
5. Escalation ladder (single public entry `interrupt_or_stop(session, deadline)`): (a) soft control_request interrupt when flag+capability allow; (b) on CapabilityMissing / FeatureDisabled / ack-timeout / ChildGone -> MT-005 supervisor graceful stop (SIGTERM semantics above, exit 143 expected); (c) supervisor hard-kill remains the supervisor's own final rung — NOT re-implemented here. The ladder is data-driven and each rung's attempt+result is recorded.
6. Undocumented-surface containment (grep-provable): the string "control_request" and the interrupt subtype literal appear ONLY in claude_interrupt.rs (constructor + tests). A unit test greps the module tree to enforce single-definition-site.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read MT-003 (capabilities), MT-004 (stdin writer), MT-005 (supervisor stop), MT-023 (injector patterns) delivered seams.
2. Implement the constructor + serde types; snapshot test the exact line.
3. Implement the gate (flag -> capability -> write -> bounded ack wait) with the closed outcome set.
4. Implement interrupt_or_stop escalation calling the MT-005 supervisor stop seam.
5. Tests: flag-off short-circuit; capability-missing short-circuit writes zero bytes (scripted child asserts no stdin traffic); happy-path write + simulated receipt -> Interrupted{acked:true}; ack-timeout -> escalation invoked; ChildGone -> escalation; single-definition-site grep test.
6. Live proof (typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF when CLI/login absent): interrupt a real long-running turn; assert the turn aborts, the session SURVIVES, and a follow-up steer (MT-023) still executes.
acceptance_criteria: claude_interrupt_request_line is the single definition site of the control_request interrupt wire shape (grep-enforced by a test); request_id is Uuid::now_v7.

Interrupt emission is double-gated: claude_interrupt_enabled flag AND interrupt_receipt_v1 capability; either gate failing yields its typed outcome with ZERO bytes written to stdin (scripted-child proven).
Bounded ack wait: receipt evidence -> Interrupted{acked:true}; timeout -> Interrupted{acked:false} and interrupt_or_stop escalates to the MT-005 supervisor graceful stop.
interrupt_or_stop escalation ladder covers CapabilityMissing, FeatureDisabled, ack-timeout, and ChildGone, each rung recorded via the MT-029 seam; no silent outcome exists.
No other undocumented control subtype is emitted, matched, or scaffolded anywhere in the diff.
Live proof (or typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF): a real mid-turn interrupt aborts the turn while the session survives and accepts a subsequent steer.
Supervisor-stop fallback proven: with the flag off, interrupt_or_stop stops the session via MT-005 SIGTERM semantics (exit 143 observed in test or live proof).
proof_targets: cargo test --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml claude_interrupt -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'
grep -rln 'control_request' src/backend/handshake_core/src/ | grep -v claude_interrupt.rs | wc -l | grep -q '^0'

LIVE (type NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF if the claude CLI or operator login is absent): interrupt a real long-running turn; assert turn abort + session survival + follow-up steer executes; separately assert supervisor SIGTERM fallback exits 143
implementation_notes: The interrupt control protocol is UNDOCUMENTED upstream (Anthropic acknowledges stream-json under-documentation in claude-code#24594); the reverse-engineered shape comes from Roasbeef claude-agent-sdk-go docs/cli-protocol.md and claude-code#41665. That is exactly why: single constructor, snapshot test, capability+flag double gate, MT-028 drift alarm, and a fallback that uses only DOCUMENTED behavior (SIGTERM -> abort turn, kill bash tree, SessionEnd hooks, exit 143).

If live testing shows the CLI emits an explicit interrupt receipt event, treat that as the ack evidence and record its observed shape in MT-028 drift notes; if only implicit evidence exists (turn ends abnormally), the acked determination uses that and says so in the outcome docs. Never fabricate an ack.
The capability string to match is exactly "interrupt_receipt_v1" from the system/init capabilities array (MT-022 ClaudeSessionInit.capabilities).
MT-005 supervisor owns process termination + ledger STOP rows (pattern: official_cli_bridge.rs terminate_and_collect usage around 2462-2490); this MT must not spawn, kill, or reap processes itself.
Session-core seams absent at implementation time = dependency-blocked (HBR-STOP-004); the only allowed stub is the no-op recording sink shared with MT-023.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Transport-layer interrupt mechanics; the operator stop/interrupt button binds to interrupt_or_stop in the WP-017 GUI MT group.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Operator/model-facing interrupt workflow docs land with the session-control tool-surface MT; this MT ships the internal escalation ladder only.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FlightRecorder: WIRED via MT-029 seam — every interrupt attempt, outcome, and escalation rung recorded.
internal_diagnostics: WIRED — closed typed outcome set (Interrupted/CapabilityMissing/FeatureDisabled/ChildGone/Escalated) inspectable per session.
Palmistry: DEFERRED-with-reason — session runtime posture owned by MT-005 supervisor + MT-029 recording; this MT contributes typed outcomes.
risk_if_missed: No graceful mid-turn stop: every abort is a SIGTERM session kill, losing session continuity (resume-only recovery), making the operator stop button destructive, and leaving the orchestrator unable to redirect a runaway worker cheaply.

risks: RISK-1: Undocumented control-protocol drift — a CLI release changes the interrupt envelope; blind emission then desynchronizes or crashes the session channel.
RISK-2: Interrupt believed delivered but never acted on (no ack evidence), leaving a runaway worker burning tokens while the harness reports it interrupted.
RISK-3: Scope creep into other undocumented control subtypes (permission prompts, mode switches) multiplying the unstable surface.
RISK-4: Fallback confusion — soft interrupt and supervisor SIGTERM race each other, double-killing or orphaning the child and corrupting ledger STOP rows.
RISK-5: Interrupt fired at a CLI without the capability corrupts the stdin channel that MT-023 steering depends on.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): single constructor + snapshot test + MT-028 live contract test = one-line fix surface; capability gate prevents blind emission.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): bounded ack wait; acked:false forces escalation to the supervisor stop — no terminal 'assumed interrupted' state.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): grep-enforced single-definition-site test; contract forbids scaffolding other subtypes.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): escalation is sequential inside interrupt_or_stop (soft rung fully resolved before supervisor rung); termination/reaping is exclusively MT-005's, which owns the ledger STOP row.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): CapabilityMissing short-circuits BEFORE any stdin write (scripted-child zero-bytes test).
